title: Activation Onramp: SentinelAI Engagement — Sprint Strategy & Success Criteria
content:
Executive summary:
This is the onramp plan for the SentinelAI activation window (4-week engagement). Goal is to run a narrow, measurable proof window that demonstrates production-feasible latency and cost for their customer-facing summarization feature and to validate our recommended Dedicated routing + prefix caching profile. This doc is practical — contains the sprint plan, workshop agenda, acceptance tests, data/security checklist, and explicit owner-level tasks.

Primary objectives (what success looks like):
- Latency: end-to-end 95th percentile generation latency <= 500ms for 256-token responses on target workload during 20 RPS sustained traffic on Dedicated pool.
- Cost: per-token inference cost reduction >= 35% vs baseline (customer's current endpoint) using caching + quantized model variant without perceptible quality drop.
- Quality: Rouge-L and human spot-checks show <= 5% degradation against baseline for extractive summary quality on a 200-sample eval set.
- Reliability: 99.9% successful responses over the proof window (errors < 0.1%).
- Ops: Canary rollout and automatic fallback validated end-to-end with documented runbook.

Constraints & assumptions:
- Customer will provide a 1 TB sample data bundle (aggregated logs and a 10k document sample) by Day -3.
- Network: VPC peering is approved and test VPN credentials are available no later than Day 0.
- We are running Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2 region.
- Default model family for evaluation: small-LlamaX-8q (quantized variant) with Redwood-verified kernels.

Sprint timeline (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (Prep, Days -7 to -1):
  - Deliverables: test data ingest script, initial config YAML, security questionnaire answered, access granted to Sentinel engineering sandbox.
  - Owners: Priya (SE lead) to coordinate access; Marcus (infra) to provision Dedicated cores.
- Week 1 (Orientation & Baseline):
  - Tasks: baseline measurement against customer's current endpoint, run baseline eval harness (200 samples), initial deploy of model variant in a non-production namespace.
  - Deliverables: baseline latency/cost table, initial eval report.
- Week 2 (Optimization & Workshop):
  - Tasks: enable prefix/KV caching, tune batching windows, test quantization profiles, run mid-engagement quality review with customer.
  - Deliverables: optimized config, comparison report showing cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Week 3 (Scale & Resilience):
  - Tasks: ramp to 20 RPS sustained, run failure injection (network hiccup + model OOM scenarios), validate fallback routing to a smaller model.
  - Deliverables: stress test logs, fault injection report, runbook updates.
- Week 4 (Acceptance & Handover):
  - Tasks: collect final metrics, run final human evaluation, review contract extension options and Dedicated capacity sizing recommendations.
  - Deliverables: acceptance checklist signed by customer, handoff doc for customer success.

Workshop: two half-day sessions (Week 2)
- Day A (AM): Tech orientation + architecture walkthrough (20–30 min), live baseline demo (30 min), hands-on sandbox pairing (60 min).
- Day A (PM): Metrics deep-dive (token accounting, latency heatmaps), config walkthrough (batching, cache TTL, quantization).
- Day B (AM): Failure scenarios and operational runbook review, canary strategy and rollback drills.
- Day B (PM): Customer feedback session + prioritization of tweaks to be implemented during Week 3.

Roles & responsibilities (explicit owners):
- SE lead: Priya Patel — overall engagement owner, customer communication, acceptance criteria sign-off.
- Platform infra: Marcus Li — provisioning Dedicated pool, autoscale policy setup, SSH/debug access for sandbox.
- Runtime engineering: Diego Ramos — kernel selection, quantization profile recommendations, assist with performance regressions.
- CS/Program: Leah O'Connor — contract touchpoints, demo coordination, success metrics alignment with business stakeholders.
- Customer counterpart: Elena Moretti (Sentinel) — data owner, product SME, acceptance approver.

Acceptance tests (must pass for formal sign-off):
1) Performance test: 10k-sample synthetic traffic (mix of short/long prompts) at 20 RPS for 15 minutes sustained. Measured 95th latency <= 500ms.
2) Cost delta: aggregated per-token cost report (Redwood billing view vs baseline) showing >= 35% reduction.
3) Quality gate: automated eval (ROUGE-L) + 20 human spot checks with <5% performance regression.
4) Reliability gate: error budget not exceeded (errors <0.1%).
5) Security gate: data handling checklist signed; KMS access validated; audit logs enabled and retained for 30 days.

Data & security checklist (minimum):
- Data anonymization script present and run for training/eval sets (customer to confirm).
- KMS integration validated for key usage; HSM optional pending legal sign-off.
- Network: VPC peering or private link in place; no public egress for customer data during proof window.
- Logging: token-level logging disabled unless explicit consent; only latency and token counts aggregated.
- Compliance notes: customer is in scope for SOC2-lite review; security artifacts required before handoff.

Deployment plan (technical steps):
1) Create dedicated namespace + node pool in us-west-2.
2) Build model artifact with quantization profile Q3 and upload to private registry.
3) Deploy canary (5% traffic) with autoscaling min=2 max=8.
4) Monitor for 1 hour, if metrics OK, ramp to 50% then 100%.
5) Run fallback test: disable the model and confirm routing to fallback model succeeds within 3s with correct error surface.

Key risks and mitigations:
- Risk: model quality drop after quantization. Mitigation: maintain non-quantized variant for canary; human eval gating.
- Risk: unexpected OOM at peak. Mitigation: conservative memory headroom, failure injection beforehand, autoscale buffers.
- Risk: delayed data delivery from customer. Mitigation: synthetic proxies for early benchmarks; postpone heavy eval to Week 2 if necessary.

Communication plan:
- Daily 15-min standups (M–F) during Weeks 1–3. Slack channel: #se-sentinelai (invite list updated).
- Weekly status digest sent Fridays to stakeholders (Priya to own).
- Escalation: on-call infra pager (primary: Marcus; backup: Diego).

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Customer to confirm sample distribution breakdown (what % are long-form vs short prompts) — Elena action. (JIRA: SE-4123)
- Legal to confirm DPA amendments for log retention (Legal ticket: LEG-2219).
- Confirm if customer wants token-level logging for debugging (opt-in) — decision due Day 0.

Immediate next steps (within 48 hours):
- Priya: send onboarding email with data transfer instructions and requested access.
- Marcus: provision Dedicated sandbox with 2 initial GPU nodes and share SSH bastion details.
- Diego: prepare quantization bench script and baseline eval harness.
- Elena (customer): share sample data archive and network info.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep workshop lean — customers get overwhelmed by too many knobs. Prioritize the two levers that matter: caching and batch sizing.
- Bring a short recording of a rollback to show confidence during Day B.
- If time is tight, prefer to demonstrate cost improvements on a synthetic 1k-doc bucket rather than try huge archive ingest.

Appendix (links & quick references):
- Baseline measurement template: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example
- Runbook template (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Runbooks
- Perf harness README: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness#sentinel

Status: draft — ready for review by Marcus and Diego.

Signed-off-by: Priya Patel, Solutions Engineering
